title: Predicting genetic interactions across backgrounds and environments

concept.text: The innovation would be a reliable causal framework for predicting how combinations of genetic variants change a defined trait, including effects that cannot be obtained by adding the effects of individual variants. Such dependence between variants is called epistasis. Higher-order epistasis involves combinations of three or more variants, whose joint effect cannot be fully represented by single-variant and pairwise effects. The intended capability would predict previously untested combinations and quantify uncertainty, rather than require an exhaustive experimental catalogue of every genotype.

Proposed scope: predictions would transfer across specified genetic backgrounds and environments, extending from coding sequences and splice sites to interactions between genes, molecular pathways and organismal traits. Genetic background means the other variants already present in the system; a useful prediction must account for how they alter the effect of an introduced change. Environmental transfer and broad organismal prediction are objectives of this innovation, not capabilities established by the supplied studies. The goal is a predictive model for defined domains, not a literal map of every interaction or an explanation of all phenotypic variation.

significance.text: If achieved, this capability would make combinations of variants predictable where additive reasoning fails. Researchers could choose experiments that distinguish competing explanations, identify combinations likely to produce a desired molecular outcome, and iteratively improve predictions using new measurements. The 2022 study provides a bounded example of the technical basis for this approach: modeling higher-order sequence effects can support prediction and guide further experimental acquisition in defined sequence-function systems.

Conditional impact synthesis: reliable causal transfer to organismal traits would substantially change experimental genetics and trait engineering. It could help researchers select combinations of changes whose effects depend on the recipient background, assess when a combination is likely to fail, and direct measurement toward cases where uncertainty matters most. Applications to crop improvement or genetic medicine would additionally require effective interventions, delivery where relevant, and validation of the intended outcome and unintended effects. Predictive accuracy alone would not establish a successful therapy or an engineered organism that performs as intended.

Impact limits: a general framework would still operate within specified traits, interventions, backgrounds and environments. It would not eliminate environmental variation, developmental chance, measurement error or effects of factors omitted from the model. Strong average relationships between molecular and genetic interactions also need not yield accurate predictions for individual combinations. Consequently, neither a comprehensive-looking interaction network nor success on a finite benchmark would by itself establish universal organismal prediction.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability is accurate prediction outside the combinations already measured, with uncertainty that remains informative as genetic context changes. Possible sequences and variant combinations grow exponentially, making exhaustive measurement impractical. Higher-order effects add structure that simpler models can miss, while sparse observations can leave many alternative explanations consistent with the data. A useful approach must learn enough of that structure to generalize without treating unmeasured combinations as if they were already understood.

A further barrier is connecting molecular mechanisms to individual genetic outcomes. Protein interactions can help explain patterns of epistasis, but a strong relationship after averaging many interactions does not establish strong prediction of each interaction. The 2026 analysis considers pairwise deletions or knockdowns and acknowledges additional mechanisms; its reconstructed network explains only a small fraction of the variance across negative genetic interactions. Extending such findings to higher-order combinations, diverse variant types and organismal traits requires substantially more explanatory and predictive coverage.

Engineering synthesis: the broader breakthrough would require models and experiments that distinguish causal effects from associations, separate measurement noise from uncertainty due to missing knowledge, and identify when transfer to a new background or environment is unreliable. Controlled environmental transfer, integration across molecular and organismal scales, and appropriate refusal to predict remain concrete requirements of the proposed capability. The supplied studies do not establish these extensions; that evidence gap does not show they are impossible.

current_state.text: Juannan Zhou, Mandy S. Wong, Wei-Chia Chen, Adrian R. Krainer, Justin B. Kinney and David M. McCandlish published Higher-order epistasis and phenotypic prediction on 21 September 2022, DOI 10.1073/pnas.2204233119. The study presents empirical variance component regression that accommodates all interaction orders while accounting for measurement noise and predictive uncertainty. Its applications concern the GB1 protein domain and human SMN1 splice-site sequences. These demonstrate prediction in defined sequence-function settings, rather than a general causal model of whole-organism traits across backgrounds and environments.

The 2022 study also experimentally tested 40 previously unmeasured splice-site sequences. The reported agreement with the additional measurements was qualitative, with systematic discrepancies: predictions smoothed the transition between low and high splicing activity. This is meaningful prospective validation within a specified molecular system, but it should not be described as unrestricted quantitative validation. Accommodating all interaction orders in a model likewise does not mean that every individual higher-order interaction has been separately measured or resolved.

Xavier Castellanos-Girouard, Adrian W. R. Serohijos and Stephen W. Michnick published Protein-protein interactions are a major source of epistasis in genetic interaction networks, DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-69152-2. The publication history lists 5 February 2026 as the initial publication date and 12 March 2026 as the version-of-record date. The study analyzes existing yeast and human-cell datasets relating pairwise genetic interactions to protein interactions. Strong trends in binned averages do not translate into comparable predictive power for individual interactions: the reconstructed network explains approximately 2% of the entire variance in the negative genetic-interaction network. This result concerns pairwise perturbations and does not demonstrate general higher-order organismal prediction or transfer across environments. The supplied record does not establish that every detail in the retained version was already present on the initial publication date.

The supplied review had the complete 12-page main article for the 2022 study, without its separate supplement, and full main-text versions of the 2026 study. These supersede the earlier account of abstract-only access and an unverified 2022 author list. The review assessed reported results through the prose; it did not independently inspect figure images or raw data. Some equations in the 2026 PDF were extracted imperfectly, and the source index reports missing extractable text and extraction warnings in one supplementary PDF. These limitations constrain independent assessment of equations and supplementary material, while leaving the reviewed prose findings available.

Coverage limitation: these are dated examples of demonstrated progress, not an established complete account of the field through 1 November 2026. Although the reconciled research described searches through that date, the supplied freshness record is empty. The evidence therefore supports the specific studies and their bounded achievements, without establishing that no more recent or broader result exists.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: predict quantitative effects for independently chosen, previously untested combinations spanning multiple loci, genetic backgrounds and environments, for multiple well-defined traits in more than one organism. Register the predictions before measurement and validate them with controlled genetic perturbations and held-out populations. Define the intended domain and the trait measurements clearly enough that success has an interpretable biological meaning.
completion_criteria.label: Preregistered predictions validate untested multilocus combinations across biological contexts

completion_criteria.text: Proposed evaluation: set accuracy, uncertainty-coverage and transfer criteria in advance, using data splits that prevent leakage across the backgrounds and environments being tested. Compare with additive models and simpler interaction models under comparable data conditions. Evaluate both prediction error and whether stated uncertainty matches observed error, including predefined cases in which the model should declare insufficient knowledge. The supplied evidence motivates prediction with uncertainty and comparison to simpler models; these broader acceptance criteria are proposals, not established field standards.
completion_criteria.label: Leakage-free evaluation tests predefined accuracy, uncertainty-coverage and transfer criteria

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: independent groups should reproduce the principal predictions using documented perturbations, measurements and analysis procedures. Evaluation should distinguish performance within familiar systems from transfer to new backgrounds, environments and trait classes, and report the experimental burden and computational resources required. Passing would establish demonstrated breadth within the tested domains. It would not prove literal universality, explain all residual variation or establish long-term evolutionary prediction.
completion_criteria.label: Independent replication reports transfer limits and full resource costs

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: GEN-01, A predictive, causal map of the genome’s regulatory code, overlaps where regulatory variants interact to alter expression or downstream traits. GEN-11 also includes coding changes, splice-site effects, interactions between genes and pathways, and transfer across backgrounds and environments. These are complementary emphases. The supplied roster provides GEN-01’s title but not its full definition, so the precise boundary cannot be settled here.

Roster-based synthesis: GEN-02, Design and construct complex eukaryotic genomes to specification, could use GEN-11 predictions to choose combinations expected to meet a design objective. GEN-03, Precise, programmable replacement of large genomic regions in existing cells, could provide a way to install and test such combinations. GEN-04, A retargetable delivery platform for genetic medicines across the body, addresses reaching the relevant cells. Predicting a combination’s effects, constructing or replacing its sequence, and delivering an intervention are distinct capabilities; progress in one does not establish the others.

Roster-based synthesis: GEN-05, General laws of environmentally induced, sequence-independent inheritance, concerns transmission of effects without a sequence change. GEN-11’s proposed environmental scope concerns how genetic combinations affect a trait under different conditions; it does not by itself explain inheritance of environmentally induced states. GEN-08, Reconstructing an organism’s cell divisions and histories from inherited molecular marks, concerns inference of past cellular events. Such histories could provide useful context for trait studies, but reconstructing a lineage and predicting the causal effect of a variant combination remain different tasks.

Roster-based synthesis: GEN-06, Transferable clonal seed reproduction across major crops, concerns establishing a particular reproductive capability across crop species. Genetic-interaction prediction might help identify compatible combinations or background-dependent failures, but it would not itself demonstrate clonal seed reproduction. GEN-07, Predictably controllable inheritance in wild populations, concerns population inheritance and control. Predictions of individual genetic effects could inform it, while ecological conditions, population dynamics and controllability would still require separate evidence.

Roster-based synthesis: GEN-09, An autonomous, evolvable expanded genetic alphabet, concerns sustaining and evolving an enlarged molecular alphabet. GEN-11 could potentially help characterize interactions among changes in such a system, but the supplied results do not establish transfer beyond their tested sequence systems. GEN-10, A testable reconstruction of the origin and fixation of the genetic code, concerns historical explanation. Predicting present-day combinations would neither reconstruct that history nor establish why a particular code became fixed.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish predictive transfer across controlled environments or broad organismal traits; the extent of achievable transfer remains open.
The empty freshness record leaves comprehensive coverage through 1 November 2026 unverified.
GEN-01’s full definition is absent, so its exact boundary with GEN-11 remains unresolved despite the supplied title and research description.

Numerical acceptance thresholds, trait choices, organism choices and practical resource limits for a convincing demonstration remain to be specified; no consensus thresholds are established by this record.
The supplied record does not establish which details of the 2026 retained article were present at initial publication on 5 February rather than by the version of record on 12 March.
Independent assessment of figures, raw data and incompletely extracted supplementary content remains outside the supplied review’s demonstrated inspection scope.

brief.title: Predicting what combinations of DNA changes will do
possible: Researchers could predict what combinations of DNA changes would cause, even when their effects do not simply add up. Predictions would account for the other variants already present and the environment, and say how uncertain they are.
They could assess combinations that have never been tested, without measuring every possibility. The goal would cover defined traits, from molecular activity to characteristics of whole organisms.
why: Researchers could choose genetic changes more likely to produce a desired result and identify combinations likely to fail. They could also focus experiments on the unknowns that matter most, using each measurement to improve the next prediction.

sources.showed: They built a model that predicts molecular effects of DNA combinations and estimates uncertainty. It accommodates interactions involving any number of changes and was applied to protein binding and RNA splicing, the editing of gene messages.
sources.quote:
Here we present a method for reconstructing sequence-to-function mappings
from partially observed data that can accommodate all orders of genetic interaction.
sources.cited_for: Interactions among multiple DNA changes can help predict the effects of untested combinations.
sources.not_established: The work does not establish reliable prediction of whole-organism traits across genetic backgrounds and environments.

sources.who: Xavier Castellanos-Girouard, Adrian W. R. Serohijos and Stephen W. Michnick
sources.showed: They linked protein binding to the combined effects of disrupting pairs of genes in yeast and human cells. Despite strong average trends, their reconstructed network explained about 2% of variation in interactions where combined disruptions caused extra harm.
sources.quote: Consequently, we show that genetic interaction and protein-protein interaction networks can reciprocally predict each other.
sources.cited_for: Physical interactions between proteins help explain patterns in how gene disruptions combine.
sources.not_established: Strong average relationships do not establish accurate predictions for individual combinations or interactions involving larger groups of genes.

shown: Zhou and colleagues tested predictions on 40 previously unmeasured sequences involved in RNA splicing. The measurements broadly agreed with predictions, but the model blurred the transition between low and high activity. This demonstrates useful prediction within a defined molecular system.
missing: Accurate predictions for untested combinations as the surrounding genetic variants change, with uncertainty that remains trustworthy.
Controlled demonstrations that predictions transfer across environments and extend to whole-organism traits.
Models that distinguish causal effects from associations and recognize when they lack enough knowledge to predict.

milestones.label: Advance predictions succeed across organisms, traits and environments
milestones.explanation: Predictions registered before measurement would have to pass controlled tests of independently chosen, untested combinations across traits, organisms, genetic backgrounds and environments. This would establish breadth beyond familiar systems.

milestones.label: Fair tests confirm accuracy, uncertainty and transfer
milestones.explanation: Tests excluding overlap with training data would have to meet preset accuracy, uncertainty and transfer criteria against simpler models, including when to withhold predictions. This would establish dependable performance.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce results and report limits and costs
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce predictions with documented procedures, separating familiar-system success from transfer and reporting experimental and computing costs. This would establish practical breadth within tested domains.

uncertain: How far can predictions transfer to unfamiliar genetic backgrounds, environments and whole-organism traits?
Which accuracy thresholds, traits, organisms and resource limits would make a demonstration convincing?

page.title: Epistasis prediction across genetic backgrounds and environments
page.definition: Models predict how untested combinations of DNA variants change a specified trait across stated genetic backgrounds and environments, with predictive uncertainty. They capture epistasis, departures from a specified no-interaction model, including interactions among three or more variants; genetic background means the other variants present.

goal.need: Four variable GB1 protein positions admit 160,000 amino-acid combinations. Mutational-effect correlations in this system fall from 0.72 between backgrounds one substitution apart to 0.32 between backgrounds three substitutions apart. A 2026 reconstruction from protein interactions explained approximately 2% of variance in a yeast negative genetic-interaction network. These results motivate predicting individual combinations and their context dependence without exhaustive measurement.

completion.title: Independent experiments validate epistasis predictions in new genetic backgrounds and environments.
completion.criterion: A model fixed before testing predicts effects of unmeasured variant combinations, including combinations of three or more variants, on one specified trait in one organism, in genetic backgrounds and environments excluded from training. Independent perturbation experiments reproduce lower mean squared error than matched additive and pairwise-only models fitted to the same training data. Prediction intervals attain coverage consistent with their stated probabilities within sampling uncertainty. Achievement applies to the declared domain.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas fallback; no external body located defines a joint acceptance test for this capability.
completion.basis: Searches of NSF EDGE and ORCC targets, epistasis prediction papers, sequence-function benchmarks, DREAM challenges and genetic-perturbation benchmarks found no joint completion threshold. The programme statements establish prediction across contexts as a goal. This fallback confines achievement to one declared domain and requires independent prospective validation; it is not an externally adopted standard.

milestones.title: A predicted double mutant shows a visible growth defect relative to its single-mutant controls.
milestones.criterion: Construct the predicted double mutant and its corresponding single mutants. In the specified medium, the double mutant must have a visually apparent growth defect relative to the single mutants in a plate-growth assay. Harrison et al.'s report dated 13 February 2007 found the predicted synthetic-sick or lethal phenotype in 12 of 17 newly tested gene-pair–medium cases.
milestones.set_by: Harrison et al., Table 1 experimental-validation protocol in Plasticity of genetic interactions in metabolic networks of yeast; written for budding-yeast metabolic gene deletions.
milestones.threshold_quote: considered successful if the double mutant had a visually apparent growth defect compared with single mutants in a plate growth assay

milestones.title: A model predicts held-out variant combinations with lower mean squared error than an additive model.
milestones.criterion: Within one specified experimental system and trait scale, predictions for combinations excluded from fitting have lower mean squared error than an additive model trained on the same measurements. Zhou et al., published on 21 September 2022, reported held-out comparisons against additive, pairwise and three-way models for GB1 protein binding. Such comparisons establish within-system predictive performance rather than environmental transfer.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas fallback; searches of sequence-function prediction papers and benchmarks found model comparisons but no externally adopted acceptance threshold for this stage.

milestones.title: Prospective combination predictions have lower error than additive and pairwise-only models.
milestones.criterion: Predictions fixed before new measurements of variant combinations have lower mean squared error than matched additive and pairwise-only models in the same assay. On 21 September 2022, Zhou et al. reported testing 40 unmeasured SMN1 splice-site sequences in three replicates each. Agreement was qualitative; measured splicing changed more abruptly than predicted. That validation does not establish this comparative acceptance test.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas fallback; searches of prospective epistasis-validation studies found no published general acceptance threshold against both additive and pairwise-only prediction.

milestones.title: Joint background and environment holdouts show lower error than additive and pairwise-only models.
milestones.criterion: In existing perturbation data, withhold target genetic backgrounds and environments together. Predictions of combination effects must have lower mean squared error than matched additive and pairwise-only models, with interval coverage consistent with stated probabilities. Li and Zhang, published on 23 April 2018, measured 23,284 yeast tRNA genotypes in four environments and transferred fitness predictions using measurements of some genotypes in the target environment. This supports environmental adaptation, but does not establish the joint holdout test.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas fallback; searches of multi-environment fitness-landscape studies and genomic prediction benchmarks found no joint acceptance threshold for epistasis, background transfer and uncertainty calibration.

not_found: No external completion test was found combining higher-order interaction prediction, genetic-background transfer, environmental transfer and predictive-uncertainty calibration.
No externally adopted pass thresholds were found for the three Atlas-defined predictive milestones.
The cited results do not establish independent prospective validation under jointly excluded genetic backgrounds and environments.
